# Exploratory Data Analysis

The 72,856 sessions span multiple months and include 2,337 users, averaging 31.2 sessions per user annually. Total energy consumed was 1.27 million kWh, with average session energy of 17.44 kWh. Session durations averaged 2.52 hours, showing right-skewed distribution with many short sessions and fewer long ones.


## Temporal Patterns

Arrival time analysis revealed a clear evening peak. Hours 17:00-20:00 account for 20-25% of all arrivals, with 18:00 being the busiest hour (4,063 sessions, 5.6%). This aligns with grid peak demand periods, creating V2G opportunities.

However, depature patterns introduce constraints. Morning depatures (05:00-10:00) represent 16.4% of sessions (11,915 total). These users require full charge completion by early morning, limiting overnight V2G participation. This impacts the overall V2G availability rate.

![Arrival and Depature Patterns](figures/eda_nature_user_patterns.png)

*Figure 1: User behaviour patterns showing arrival times (top left), depature time (top right), session duration distribution (middle left), V2G availability by hour (middle right), location analysis (bottom left), and user clustering (bottom right).*


## Session Duration Analysis

Session duration were categorized to understand V2G potential:

- **Short Sessions (< 2h)**: 37,972 sessions (52.1%)
  - Quick charging scenarios
  - Limited V2G potential due to insufficient idle time

- **Medium Session (2-8h)**: 31,716 session (43.5%)
  - Work/shopping scenarios
  - Primary V2G opportunity window

- **Long Sessions (> 8h)**: 3,168 sessions (4.3%)
  - Overnight charging
  - High V2G potential but constrained by morning depature requirements


### V2G Opportunity Analysis

Critical finding: average idle time per session is only 0.53 hours. Most users disconnect shortly after charging completes, leaving minimal window for V2G discharge. Only 3,724 sessions and > 2 hours of idle time meeting V2G eligibility criteria.

This low percentage was a surprise intially. While many users charge during peak hours, few have sufficient post-charging idle periods. This suggests V2G program must target specific user segments rather than universal participation.


## Location-Based Analysis

Location analysis reveals signficant variation in V2G potential:

| Location | Sessions | Avg Duration | V2G Availability |
|----------|----------|--------------|------------------|
| Apartment | 14,038 | 3.4h | **10.4%** |
| Public Area | 14,082 | 2.2h | 3.0% |
| Resort | 8,854 | 2.8h | 4.2% |
| Hotel | 8,600 | 2.4h | 3.7% |
| Company | 7,558 | 2.5h | 4.2% |
| Public Institution | 7,023 | 2.0h | 5.3% |
| Market | 3,005 | 1.6h | 6.0% |
| Restaurant | 2,222 | 2.6h | 5.8% |
| Camping | 1,630 | 4.1h | 1.5% |
| Public Parking Lot | 3,396 | 0.8h | 1.6% |

This finding suggests targeted deployment strategies like focusing V2G infrastructure on apartments could yield higher participation rates than broad deployment.

## User Clustering
Clustering users by behaviour patterns revealed distinct segments.
"Evening chargers"(21.7% of users, 506 total) arrive around 19:30 with average 3.4 hour sessions. This segment shows highest V2G potential due to peak hour arrivals and sufficient duration. "Work chargers" (09:00-17:00 arrivals) show moderate potential, while "overnight chargers" are constrained by morning depature requirements.

## Grid-User Integration Analysis

Integration of grid data with user patterns reveals the optimal V2G window:

![Grid-User Integration Analysis](figures/GridandUserData_integration_analysis.png)

*Figure 2: Integration analysis showing hourly opportunity scores (top left), grid vs. user availability (top right), and composite V2G opportunity scores combining grid needs with user behaviour patterns.*

Combining grid and user data identified the optimal 4-hour window: 17:00-20:00. During these hours, composite scores reach 100/100, indicating perfect alignment between grid needs (high prices, high demand) and user availability(peak arrivals. sufficient durations). Hours outside this window score < 40, making V2G economically unviable.
